name: Ramp
text:
Add a **large, high-contrast skip link** at the top of every page, visible by default.

This ensures keyboard users bypass repetitive navigation blocks in one click, solving a core keyboard navigation failure. The trade-off is a small permanent visual element, but its size and contrast make it unobtrusive while remaining usable.

name: Reader
text: A large, always-visible skip link steals focus from the main content for sighted users and risks being ignored as visual noise. A better alternative is a skip link that only appears on keyboard focus, but we must test it with screen readers to confirm it’s discoverable without sighted cues. Settle this by running a quick keyboard-only test with NVDA/JAWS and measuring if users can reach the main content in ≤2 keystrokes.

The trade-off is we must test with screen readers to confirm discoverability, but that’s a small cost compared to the benefit of keeping the interface clean while fixing a critical accessibility barrier.

name: Reader
text: A skip link that only appears on focus risks being invisible to screen-reader users who don’t know it exists—unless we test it with real screen-reader users and confirm they can discover it via keyboard navigation. A safer alternative is a skip link that’s always visible but small and tucked away (like top-right), so it’s discoverable without stealing focus from main content. Settle this by testing both versions with screen readers and keyboard users—if the hidden version fails discoverability, we default to the small, always-visible one.
